summary: Set up a LUKS-encrypted, file-backed volume on node1 mounted at /srv/secure with automated unlock and mount at boot via a systemd oneshot service, then validated it survives a real reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL 7.9, systemd 219) disk layout — no spare partition/disk existed, so used a 2GB file-backed image (/etc/cryptvolumes/secure.img) as the encrypted backing store
Confirmed cryptsetup was already present (/usr/sbin/cryptsetup, not on default PATH) after adding a CentOS-7 vault repo and running yum install (no-op since already installed)
Generated a 512-byte random keyfile on-node (/etc/cryptvolumes/secure.key, mode 400) via /dev/urandom for unattended unlock
LUKS1-formatted a loop device backed by the image file, opened it as /dev/mapper/secure, created an ext4 filesystem, mounted at /srv/secure, and wrote a test file

Because systemd 219's crypttab doesn't support file-backed loop devices directly, wrote /usr/local/sbin/secure-volume-mount.sh (finds/creates the loop device, luksOpen with keyfile, mounts) plus systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/secure-volume.service (DefaultDependencies=no, Before=local-fs.target, WantedBy=local-fs.target) and enabled it
Fixed a losetup flag incompatibility in the script (old util-linux lacks --noheadings/--output/-n), verified idempotent manual start/stop cycles worked

Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service active, mount healthy, data present, LUKS status active), triggered 'shutdown -r now' in the background so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, and confirmed boot_id changed (95e2f83d... -> 7b22e416...)

Verified post-reboot: secure-volume.service auto-started and succeeded, /srv/secure mounted from /dev/mapper/secure (ext4), test file content intact, cryptsetup status showed the LUKS mapping active — all without manual intervention

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume mounted at /srv/secure exists and works
evidence.summary: Created file-backed image, generated keyfile, LUKS-formatted a loop device, opened it, created ext4, mounted at /srv/secure, and wrote/read a test file confirming functional encrypted storage.

evidence.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts on its own at boot (automation setup)
evidence.summary: Created and enabled secure-volume.service plus the mount script, fixed a losetup compatibility bug, and confirmed systemctl start succeeds and mounts /srv/secure with prior data intact.
Captured boot_id 95e2f83d-06d0-47d9-8151-0f56c34060f1, service active, mount healthy, data present, and cryptsetup status active before reboot.
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' so the exec call acknowledged (REBOOT_TRIGGERED) before the node dropped.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Node1 became unreachable (connection timed out) then came back with boot_id 7b22e416-f2cf-4e91-ba92-09e52231512d, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, with uptime 0 minutes confirming a fresh boot.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: volume auto-unlocked, mounted, and data intact without manual action
evidence.summary: After reboot, secure-volume.service was active/exited successfully, /srv/secure was mounted from /dev/mapper/secure (ext4), the test file content was intact, and cryptsetup status showed the LUKS mapping active — all automatic.
